value.zh: 自頃甿俗巧偽，乃至竊注爵位，盜易年月，增損三狀，貿襲萬端。
value.en: Recently common people have grown cunning and false, even secretly entering titles and ranks, illicitly altering years and months, increasing and decreasing the three descriptions, and exchanging and usurping in countless ways.
value.literal: Recently common people's customs have become cunning and false, even to the point of secretly entering titles and ranks, illicitly altering years and months, increasing and decreasing the three descriptions, and exchanging and usurping in ten thousand ways.

value.zh: 或戶存而文書已絕，或人在而反托死叛，停私而云隸役，身強而稱六疾。
value.en: In some cases the household remains but the documents have vanished; in some the person is alive yet falsely claims death or flight; some remain privately while claiming to be in service, and some are healthy yet claim the six illnesses.
value.literal: In some cases the household remains but the documents have already vanished; in some the person is alive yet falsely claims death or flight; some remain privately while claiming to be in service, and some are healthy yet claim the six illnesses.

value.zh: 此皆政之巨蠹，教之深疵。
value.en: These are all grave pests in government and deep flaws in instruction.
value.literal: These are all great worms in government and deep flaws in instruction.

value.zh: 若約之以刑，則人偽已遠，若綏之以德，則勝殘未易。
value.en: If they are restrained by punishments, the people's falsity has already gone far; if they are soothed by virtue, overcoming the remaining evil will not be easy.
value.literal: If they are restrained by punishments, the people's falsity has already gone far; if they are soothed by virtue, overcoming the remnant evil will not be easy.

value.zh: 諸賢並深明政體，各獻嘉謀。」
value.en: You worthies all deeply understand the structure of government; each of you should offer excellent plans."
value.literal: You worthies all deeply understand the structure of government; each of you should offer excellent plans."

value.zh: 玩之表言便宜，多見採納。
value.en: Wanzhi submitted a memorial discussing suitable measures, and many of them were adopted.
value.literal: Wanzhi submitted a memorial discussing suitable measures, and many of them were adopted.

value.zh: 於是朝廷乃別置校籍官，置令史，限人一日得數巧，以防懈怠。
value.en: Thereupon the court separately established officials for checking registers and appointed clerks, limiting the number of register frauds each person could process in one day to guard against slackness.
value.literal: Thereupon the court separately established officials for checking registers and appointed clerks, limiting the number of deceptions each person could process in one day to guard against slackness.

value.zh: 既連年不已，貨賄潛通，百姓怨望。
value.en: After this continued year after year without end, bribes circulated secretly, and the common people grew resentful.
value.literal: After this continued year after year without end, bribes and gifts circulated secretly, and the common people were resentful.

value.zh: 十年四月癸丑，崇賢殿災。
value.en: On the guichou day of the fourth month of the tenth year fire destroyed the Chongxian Hall.
value.literal: On the guichou day of the fourth month of the tenth year, the Chongxian Hall burned.

value.zh: 十月庚辰，含章鞠室、脩成堂前廡、丙坊東屋、煇章殿南閣火。
value.en: On the gengchen day of the tenth month fire broke out in the Hanzhang kickball court, the front veranda of the Xiucheng Hall, the eastern rooms of the Bing Ward, and the southern wing of the Huizhang Hall.
value.literal: On the gengchen day of the tenth month, fire struck the Hanzhang cuju court, the front colonnade of the Xiucheng Hall, the eastern rooms of the Bing Ward, and the southern gallery of the Huizhang Hall.

value.zh: 時有上書者曰：「漢王氏五侯兄弟迭任，今楊氏三公並在大位。
value.en: A memorialist wrote at the time, "Under Han the five Wang marquises held office in turn; now the three Yang dukes all stand at the summit of power together.
value.literal: At the time a memorialist said: "Under Han the five marquises of the Wang clan held office in succession as brothers; now the three dukes of the Yang clan all hold high position together.

value.zh: 天變屢見，竊為陛下憂之。」
value.en: Heavenly omens keep appearing, and I cannot help fearing for Your Majesty."
value.literal: Heavenly changes appear repeatedly; I venture to be anxious on Your Majesty's behalf."

value.zh: 楊珧由是乞退。
value.en: Yang Yao thereupon asked to withdraw from office.
value.literal: Yang Yao therefore requested to retire.

value.zh: 是時帝納馮紞之間，廢張華之功；
value.en: At that time the emperor heeded Feng Dan's private advice and cast aside Zhang Hua's merits;
value.literal: At that time the emperor accepted Feng Dan's private counsel and set aside Zhang Hua's achievements;

value.zh: 聽楊駿之讒，離衞瓘之寵。
value.en: listened to Yang Jun's slanders and turned away from Wei Guan's favor.
value.literal: heeded Yang Jun's slanders and estranged himself from Wei Guan's favor.

value.zh: 此逐功臣之罰也。
value.en: This was the retribution for driving out worthy ministers.
value.literal: This was the penalty for expelling meritorious ministers.

value.zh: 明年，宮車晏駕。
value.en: The following year the emperor died.
value.literal: The next year the imperial carriage halted at dusk.

value.zh: 其後楚王承竊發之旨，戮害二公，身亦不免。
value.en: Later the Prince of Chu, acting on a clandestine order, killed the two chief ministers, yet could not save himself.
value.literal: Afterward the Prince of Chu, acting on a secretly issued directive, slaughtered the two grandees, yet he himself did not escape punishment.

value.zh: 震災其坊，又天意乎。
value.en: Lightning had already struck his residence—was that not Heaven's intent as well?
value.literal: Lightning had struck his ward—was this again Heaven's intent?

value.zh: 晉惠帝元康五年閏月庚寅，武庫火。
value.en: On the gengyin day of the intercalary fifth Yuankang year under Emperor Hui of Jin, fire destroyed the imperial armory.
value.literal: On the gengyin day of the intercalary month of the fifth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, the armory burned.

value.zh: 張華疑有亂，先固守，然後救災。
value.en: Zhang Hua, suspecting revolt, secured the site before turning to fight the blaze.
value.literal: Zhang Hua suspected rebellion and first held the site under guard, only then fighting the fire.

value.zh: 是以累代異寶，王莽頭，孔子履，漢高斷白蛇劍及二百萬人器械，一時蕩盡。
value.en: Thus treasures hoarded for generations—the head of Wang Mang, Confucius's sandal, the sword with which Han Gaozu slew the white serpent, and arms for two million men—were destroyed in a single hour.
value.literal: Thus rare treasures accumulated over generations—the head of Wang Mang, Confucius's shoe, the sword with which Gaozu of Han cut the white serpent, and arms for two million men—were swept away at once.

value.zh: 是後愍懷見殺，殺太子之罰也。
value.en: Later Prince Minhuai was murdered—the retribution for killing the heir apparent.
value.literal: Afterward Prince Minhuai was killed—the penalty for slaying the crown prince.

value.zh: 天戒若曰，夫設險擊柝，所以固其國，儲積戎器，所以戒不虞。
value.en: Heaven seemed to warn: ramparts and watch-clappers exist to secure the realm; arsenals are stocked to guard against surprise.
value.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: defenses and night-watch clappers are set up to secure the state; stores of weapons are amassed to guard against the unforeseen.

value.zh: 今冢嗣將傾，社稷將泯，禁兵無所復施，皇旅又將誰衞。
value.en: Now the heir's house is collapsing, the altars are failing, the palace guard can no longer be used, and who will defend the throne?
value.literal: Now the heir's line is about to topple, the altars of soil and grain about to perish; the palace guard can no longer be deployed, and who will guard the imperial host?

value.zh: 帝后不悟，終喪四海，是其應也。
value.en: Emperor and empress failed to understand, and in the end lost the realm—the omen fulfilled.
value.literal: The emperor and empress did not understand; in the end they lost all within the four seas—this was the response.

value.zh: 張華、閻纂皆曰，武庫火而氐、羌反，太子見廢，則四海可知矣。
value.en: Zhang Hua and Yan Zuan both said that when the armory burns, the Di and Qiang rise, and the heir is deposed, the fate of the empire is already clear.
value.literal: Zhang Hua and Yan Zuan both said: when the armory burns, the Di and Qiang rebel, and the crown prince is deposed—then the fate of all within the four seas can be known.

value.zh: 元康八年十一月，高原陵火。
value.en: In the eleventh month of the eighth Yuankang year fire struck the Gaoyuan Mausoleum.
value.literal: In the eleventh month of the eighth year of Yuankang, the Gaoyuan Mausoleum burned.

value.zh: 是時賈后凶恣，賈謐擅朝，惡積罪稔，宜見誅絕。
value.en: At the time Empress Jia was brutal and overbearing and Jia Mi dominated the court; their crimes had piled high and they ought to have been destroyed.
value.literal: At that time Empress Jia was fierce and unrestrained, Jia Mi monopolized the court; evil had accumulated and guilt was ripe—they ought to have been executed.

value.zh: 天戒若曰，臣妾之不可者，雖親貴莫比，猶宜忍而誅之，如吾燔高原陵也。
value.en: Heaven seemed to warn that even the closest and most exalted minister or consort, when intolerable, must be struck down—as it had burned the Gaoyuan Mausoleum.
value.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: what must not be tolerated in ministers and consorts, though none be closer or nobler, should still be endured only long enough to execute them—as I have burned the Gaoyuan Mausoleum.

value.zh: 帝既眊弱，而張華又不納裴頠、劉卞之謀，故后遂與謐誣殺太子也。
value.en: The emperor was already feeble, and Zhang Hua refused the counsel of Pei Song and Liu Bian, so the empress and Mi conspired to destroy the heir apparent.
value.literal: The emperor was already dim-eyed and weak, and Zhang Hua did not adopt the plans of Pei Song and Liu Bian, so the empress then joined with Mi to frame and kill the crown prince.

value.zh: 干寶云：「高原陵火，太子廢，其應也。
value.en: Gan Bao wrote, "Fire at the Gaoyuan Mausoleum and the heir's deposition were the same omen fulfilled.
value.literal: Gan Bao said: "When the Gaoyuan Mausoleum burned, the crown prince was deposed—this was the response.

value.zh: 漢武帝世，高園便殿火，董仲舒對與此占同。」
value.en: Under Emperor Wu of Han the Gaoyuan side hall burned, and Dong Zhongshu's interpretation matched this reading."
value.literal: In the age of Emperor Wu of Han, the side hall of the Gaoyuan burned; Dong Zhongshu's response used the same prognostication."

value.zh: 永康元年四月，壯武國有桑化為柏。
value.en: In the fourth month of the first Yongkang year a mulberry in Zhuangwu Principality turned into a cypress.
value.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongkang, in Zhuangwu Principality a mulberry tree transformed into a cypress.

value.zh: 是月，張華遇害。
value.en: That month Zhang Hua was killed.
value.literal: That month, Zhang Hua met with murder.

value.zh: 開皇九年，平陳，獲宋、齊舊樂，詔于太常置清商署以管之。
value.en: ninth year of In of Kaihuang, after Chen fell, Song and Qi court music was seized and a Qing Shang Office was set up under the Grand Music Master.
value.literal: In the ninth year of Kaihuang, after the conquest of Chen, the court acquired the old music of Song and Qi; an edict ordered the establishment of a Qing Shang Office under the Director of Ceremonies to administer it.

value.zh: 求陳太樂令蔡子元、於普明等，復居其職。
value.en: Cai Ziyuan, Yu Puming, and other former Chen music officials were found and reappointed.
value.literal: Chen's former Director of Music Cai Ziyuan, Yu Puming, and others were sought out and restored to their posts.

value.zh: 由是牛弘奏曰：
value.en: Niu Hong then submitted a memorial:
value.literal: Thereupon Niu Hong memorialized, saying:

value.zh: 晉武帝泰始二年，遣傅玄等造行禮及上壽食舉歌詩。
value.en: In second year of Jin of Taishi, Fu Xuan and others were sent to write processional, longevity, and banquet songs.
value.literal: In the second year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, Fu Xuan and others were dispatched to compose songs for processional rites, longevity toasts, and banquet music.

value.zh: 張華表曰：「按漢、魏所用，雖詩章辭異，興廢隨時，至其韻逗曲折，並系於舊，一皆因襲，不敢有所改也。」
value.en: Zhang Hua wrote: "Han and Wei pieces differ in wording and came and went with the times, but their phrasing and turns all followed old models—nothing was boldly changed."
value.literal: Zhang Hua memorialized: "Examining what Han and Wei used, although the texts of the poems differ and pieces rose and fell with the times, their cadences and turns all depend on the old models—every one was inherited, and none dared to be altered."

value.zh: 九年，荀勖典樂，使郭夏、宋識造《正德》、《大豫》之舞。
value.en: In year 9, Xun Xu had Guo Xia and Song Shi compose Correct Virtue and Great Yu.
value.literal: In the ninth year, Xun Xu oversaw music and had Guo Xia and Song Shi create the Correct Virtue and Great Yu dances."

value.zh: 改魏《昭武舞》曰《宣武舞》，羽籥舞曰《宜文舞》。
value.en: Wei's Bright Martial became Propagating Martial, and the feather-flute dance became Propagating Culture.
value.literal: The Wei Bright Martial Dance was changed to the Propagating Martial Dance, and the feather-and-flute dance to the Propagating Culture Dance.

value.zh: 江左之初，典章堙紊，賀循為太常卿，始有登歌之樂。
value.en: Early Eastern Jin law was in disarray; under He Xun as Grand Music Master, ascent hymns finally appeared.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Eastern Jin, statutes were buried in disorder; when He Xun became Director of Ceremonies, there were at last songs for the ascent hymn.

value.zh: 大寧末，阮孚等又增益之。
value.en: Late in Daning, Ruan Fu and others expanded the repertoire.
value.literal: At the end of the Daning era, Ruan Fu and others added to them further.

value.zh: 咸和間，鳩集遺逸，鄴沒胡後，樂人頗復南度，東晉因之，以具鐘律。
value.en: In Xianhe, refugees were collected; after Ye fell, musicians fled south and Eastern Jin finally had bells and pipes.
value.literal: During the Xianhe period, scattered survivors were gathered; after Ye fell to the barbarians, many musicians crossed south again, and Eastern Jin thereby acquired bells and pitch pipes.

value.zh: 太元間，破苻永固，又獲樂工楊蜀等，閑練舊樂，於是金石始備。
value.en: In Taiyuan, after Fu Yonggu was beaten, musicians like Yang Shu restored the old repertoire and metal-and-stone instruments were complete.
value.literal: During the Taiyuan period, after the defeat of Fu Yonggu, the musicians Yang Shu and others were also captured; versed in the old music, they at last completed the full ensemble of metal and stone.

value.zh: 尋其設懸音調，並與江左是同。
value.en: Their pitch arrangements matched those of the Eastern Jin.
value.literal: Examining their suspended-instrument pitch systems, they were the same as those of the Eastern Jin.

value.zh: 隋書卷七十七列傳第四十二
value.en: Book of Sui, Volume 77, Biography 42
value.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 77, Biography 42

value.zh: 昔漢氏西京，梁王建國，平臺、東苑，慕義如林。
value.en: In the days of the Han western capital and the Liang prince's founding of his realm, at Pingtai and the Eastern Park men who admired virtue gathered like trees in a forest.
value.literal: In olden days the Han western capital and the Liang prince's founding of his state—with Pingtai and Dongyuan, those who admired righteousness were as thick as a forest.

value.zh: 馬卿辭武騎之官，枚乘罷弘農之守。
value.en: Sima Xiangru left his post in the Palace Cavalry Guard, and Mei Sheng relinquished the governorship of Hongnong.
value.literal: Sima Xiangru resigned his post in the Cavalry Guard; Mei Sheng gave up the governorship of Hongnong.

value.zh: 每覽史傳，嘗切怪之，何乃脫略官榮，棲遲籓邸？
value.en: Whenever I read the historical records, I have always wondered why they would abandon official honor and settle in a prince's household.
value.literal: Whenever I read the histories, I have deeply wondered: why cast off official glory and linger in a prince's residence?

value.zh: 以今望古，方知雅志。
value.en: Looking from today back to antiquity, I finally grasp their noble purpose.
value.literal: Viewing the past from the present, I now understand their lofty intent.

value.zh: 彼二子者，豈徒然哉！
value.en: Those two men surely did not act in vain!
value.literal: Those two men—surely they were not without purpose!

value.zh: 足下博聞強記，鉤深致遠，視漢臣之三篋，似涉蒙山，對梁相之五車，若吞雲夢。
value.en: You are erudite and retentive, probing depths and reaching far; beside the Han minister's three satchels of books you seem to traverse Mount Meng, and before the Liang chancellor's five cartloads you seem to swallow Lake Yunmeng whole.
value.literal: You are broadly learned with a strong memory, probing deep and reaching far; compared with the Han minister's three satchels, it is as if crossing Mount Meng; facing the Liang chancellor's five cartloads, it is as if swallowing the Yunmeng marsh.

value.zh: 吾兄欽賢重士，敬愛忘疲，先築郭隗之宮，常置穆生之醴。
value.en: My elder brother honors the worthy and cherishes scholars with tireless devotion; he built a palace for Guo Wei and keeps sweet wine ready for Mu Sheng.
value.literal: My elder brother reveres the worthy and esteems scholars, cherishing them without tiring; he first built the palace of Guo Wei and always keeps the wine of Mu Sheng on hand.

value.zh: 今者重開土宇，更誓山河，地方七百，牢籠曲阜，城兼七十，包舉臨淄，大啟南陽，方開東閤。
value.en: Now he has reopened his domain and renewed his pledge over land and river; his territory spans seven hundred li, embracing Qufu; his cities exceed seventy, taking in Linzi; he has thrown wide the gates of Nanyang and is now opening his eastern hall to guests.
value.literal: Now he has reopened his domain and renewed his oath over the mountains and rivers; his territory extends seven hundred li, enclosing Qufu; his cities number seventy and more, embracing Linzi; he has greatly opened Nanyang and is now opening the eastern gate.

value.zh: 想得奉飛蓋，曳長裾，藉玳筵，躡珠履，歌山桂之偃蹇，賦池竹之檀欒。
value.en: I picture you riding beneath a flying canopy, trailing your long robe, seated on a tortoiseshell mat in pearl slippers, singing of mountain cassia and composing verses on the bamboo by the pool.
value.literal: I imagine you joining under a flying canopy, trailing a long robe, resting on a tortoiseshell mat, treading in pearl slippers, singing of the towering mountain cassia and composing on the lush pool bamboo.

value.zh: 其崇貴也如彼，其風流也如此，幸甚幸甚，何樂如之！
value.en: Such is his lofty station, such his elegant bearing—what good fortune, what good fortune! What pleasure could equal it!
value.literal: His lofty eminence is like that; his refinement is like this—great fortune, great fortune! What joy could compare!

value.zh: 高視上京，有懷德祖，才謝天人，多慚子建，書不盡意，寧俟繁辭。
value.en: Gazing toward the capital, I think of Dezao; my talent falls far short of heaven and earth, and I feel deeply ashamed before Zijian; words cannot say all I mean, so why multiply them?
value.literal: Looking down upon the upper capital, I miss Dezao; in talent I fall short of heaven and man; I am much ashamed before Zijian; the letter cannot exhaust my meaning—why await elaborate words?

value.zh: 一昨伏奉教書，榮貺非恆，心靈自失。
value.en: Only yesterday I received your gracious letter; the favor shown me was beyond measure, and my heart was utterly overwhelmed.
value.literal: The day before yesterday I respectfully received your instructive letter; the honor bestowed was extraordinary, and my spirit was lost within itself.

value.zh: 若乃理高《象》、《系》，管輅思而不解，事富《山海》，郭璞注而未詳。
value.en: Its reasoning rises above the Image and Judgment texts of the Changes—Guan Lu would have pondered in vain; its matter overflows the Classic of Mountains and Seas—even Guo Pu's commentary could not exhaust it.
value.literal: As for its reasoning, it surpasses the Image and Link texts of the Changes—Guan Lu would ponder without understanding; its content is richer than the Classic of Mountains and Seas—Guo Pu annotated yet could not exhaust it.

value.zh: 至於五色相宣，八音繁會，鳳鳴不足喻，龍章莫之比。
value.en: The five colors blend in harmony and the eight tones assemble in rich concord—phoenix song cannot describe it, and dragon pattern cannot match it.
value.literal: As for the five colors harmonizing and the eight tones gathering richly—phoenix song is insufficient as analogy; dragon emblems cannot compare.

value.zh: 吳劄之論《周頌》，詎盡揄揚，郢客之奏《陽春》，誰堪赴節！
value.en: When Wu Zha discoursed on the Zhou Hymns, he could not fully praise them; when the guest of Ying played "Spring in the Capital," who could keep the beat?
value.literal: Wu Zha discussing the Zhou Hymns—how could he fully extol it? The guest of Ying playing "Spring in the Capital"—who could match the measure!

value.zh: 伏惟令王殿下，稟潤天潢，承輝日觀，雅道貴于東平，文藝高於北海。
value.en: Your Highness the Illustrious Prince, nourished by the imperial lineage and shining with the sun's radiance, excels the Prince of Dongping in refined conduct and surpasses the Prince of Beihai in literary accomplishment.
value.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Highness the Illustrious Prince, nourished by the Heavenly River, inheriting radiance from Mount Ri, ranks higher in refined learning than the Prince of Dongping and surpasses the Prince of Beihai in literary art.

value.zh: 漢則馬遷、蕭望，晉則裴楷、張華，雞樹騰聲，鵷池播美，望我清塵，悠然路絕。
value.en: Han had Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; Jin had Pei Kai and Zhang Hua—your fame resounds like the rooster tree and spreads like the egret pool; looking toward my humble trail, the road between us is impossibly far.
value.literal: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wang; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua—the rooster tree resounds, the egret pool spreads fame; gazing toward my clear dust, the path is serenely cut off.

value.zh: 祖浚燕南贅客，河朔惰游，本無意于希顏，豈有心于慕藺！
value.en: Zujun is but an extra guest in the south and a lazy wanderer in the north; I never aspired to emulate Yan Hui—how could I dream of admiring Lin Xiangru!
value.literal: Zujun is a superfluous guest south of the Yan, an idle wanderer north of the River; originally I had no thought of emulating Yan Hui—how could I have a heart set on admiring Lin Xiangru!

value.zh: 未嘗聚螢映雪，懸頭刺股，讀《論》唯取一篇，披《莊》不過盈尺。
value.en: I never studied by firefly or snowlight, never hung from a beam or pricked my thigh; I read only one chapter of the Analects and barely a foot of Zhuangzi.
value.literal: I have never gathered fireflies to read by snow-light, hung my head or pricked my thigh; in reading the Analects I take only one chapter; in opening Zhuangzi I go no more than a full foot's length.

value.zh: 複況桑榆漸暮，藜藿屢空，舉燭無成，穿楊盡棄。
value.en: Moreover, sunset draws near like mulberry and elm at dusk; my larder is often bare; I have achieved nothing by lamplight and abandoned all hope of hitting the willow leaf.
value.literal: Moreover, like the mulberry and elm at dusk, I am nearing old age; greens and coarse grains are repeatedly empty; raising the candle brings no achievement; shooting through the willow is all abandoned.

value.zh: 但以燕求馬首，薛養雞鳴，謬齒鴻儀，虛班驥皁。
value.en: Yet as Yan sought the horse's head and Xue kept the rooster crowing, I have wrongly taken my place among swans and falsely ranked among thoroughbreds.
value.literal: Yet through Yan seeking the horse's head and Xue raising the rooster's crow, I wrongly count myself among the swan's ranks and vainly take place among the thoroughbred blacks.

value.zh: 挾太山而超北海，比報德而非難，堙昆侖以為池，匹酬恩而反易。
value.en: Carrying Mount Tai over the North Sea would be easier than repaying your virtue; damming Mount Kunlun to make a pool would be simpler than returning your kindness.
value.literal: To grasp Mount Tai and leap over the North Sea—compared with repaying virtue that is not hard; to dam Mount Kunlun to make a pool—matching return of kindness is instead easy.

value.zh: 忽屬周桐錫瑞，康水承家，門有將相，樹宜桃李。
value.en: Suddenly the Zhou paulownia receives its omen and the house of Kang inherits the realm; generals and ministers stand at your gate, and your trees are fit to bear peach and plum.
value.literal: Suddenly the Zhou paulownia bestows its auspice and the Kang waters inherit the house; at the gate are generals and ministers; the trees are fit for peach and plum.

value.zh: 真龍將下，誰好有名，濫吹先逃，何須別聽！
value.en: When the true dragon is about to descend, who still seeks renown? The incompetent musician has already fled—why should anyone else stay to listen!
value.literal: When the true dragon is about to descend, who will crave fame? The one who blew poorly has already fled—why need anyone else listen!

value.zh: 但慈旨抑揚，損上益下，江海所以稱王，丘陵為之不逮。
value.en: Yet your gracious words humble yourself and exalt me; rivers and seas are called kings because they lie below, and hills and mounds cannot match them.
value.literal: But your kindly words raise up the lowly and lower the lofty; it is for this that rivers and seas are called kings, and hills and mounds cannot compare.

value.zh: 曹植儻預聞高論，則不隕令名，楊修若切在下風，亦詎虧淳德。
value.en: Had Cao Zhi heard your lofty discourse, his fine name would not have fallen; had Yang Xiu stood in your shadow, his pure virtue would not have suffered.
value.literal: If Cao Zhi had chanced to hear your lofty discourse, he would not lose his fine name; if Yang Xiu were right beneath your wind, he too would not diminish pure virtue.

value.zh: 無任荷戴之至，謹奉啟以聞。
value.en: Overwhelmed with gratitude, I respectfully submit this reply for your notice.
value.literal: I cannot bear the utmost of my burdened gratitude; I respectfully submit this letter to inform you.

value.zh: 李琰之 祖瑩 常景
value.en: Li Yanzhi, Zu Ying, and Chang Jing
value.literal: Li Yanzhi, Zu Ying, Chang Jing

value.zh: 景所著述數百篇，見行於世，刪正晉司空張華博物志及撰儒林、列女傳各數十篇云。
value.en: Jing's writings numbered several hundred pieces in circulation; he revised the Jin Grand Marshal Zhang Hua's Records of Broad Learning and is said to have compiled several dozen chapters each of Biographies of Confucian Scholars and Biographies of Exemplary Women.
value.literal: Jing's compositions numbered several hundred pieces circulating in the world; he edited and corrected the Jin Grand Marshal Zhang Hua's Bowuzhi and compiled several dozen chapters each of the Rulin and Lienv Zhuan, it is said.

value.zh: 陳叔達，字子聰，陳宣帝子也。
value.en: Chen Shuda, whose courtesy name was Zicong, was a son of Emperor Xuan of Chen.
value.literal: Chen Shuda—Chen Shuda, courtesy name Zicong, was a son of Emperor Xuan of Chen.

value.zh: 少封義陽王，歷丹楊尹、都官尚書。
value.en: While still young he was made Prince of Yiyang and later held the posts of intendant of Danyang and minister of justice.
value.literal: In his youth he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang and served successively as Intendant of Danyang and Minister of Justice.

value.zh: 入隋，久不試。
value.en: When the Chen fell to the Sui he went for a long time without receiving an appointment.
value.literal: After Chen fell to the Sui, he long went without being given office.

value.zh: 大業中，授內史舍人，出為絳郡通守。
value.en: During the Daye reign he was made a secretariat gentleman and then dispatched as prefect of Jiang Commandery.
value.literal: In the Daye era he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and sent out as Administrator-General of Jiang Commandery.

value.zh: 高祖西師，以郡聽命，授丞相府主簿，封漢東郡公。
value.en: When Gaozu advanced west, the commandery submitted to him; Chen was named chief clerk in the chancellor's office and created Duke of Handong.
value.literal: When Gaozu marched west with his army, the commandery submitted on his orders; he was appointed Chief Clerk in the Chancellor's Office and enfeoffed as Duke of Handong Commandery.

value.zh: 與溫大雅同管機秘，方禪代時，書冊誥詔，皆其筆也。
value.en: He and Wen Daya jointly managed confidential records, and as the dynastic transition drew near he drafted the books, registers, and proclamations.
value.literal: Together with Wen Daya he oversaw the secret archives; when the transfer of the mandate was imminent, all books, registers, and proclamations were in his hand.

value.zh: 武德初，授黃門侍郎，判納言，封江國公。
value.en: Early in Wude he became vice minister of the palace secretariat, served concurrently as head censor, and was created Duke of Jiang.
value.literal: At the beginning of Wude he was appointed Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat, with concurrent duty as Head Censor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Jiang.

value.zh: 秦王討王世充，命倫參謀軍事。
value.en: When the Prince of Qin marched against Wang Shichong, he put Feng Lun on his staff as military adviser.
value.literal: When Prince Qin campaigned against Wang Shichong, he ordered Lun to advise on military affairs.

value.zh: 時兵久不決，帝欲班師，王遣倫西見帝曰：「賊地雖多，羈縻不相使，所用命者洛陽爾，計窮力屈，死在旦暮。
value.en: The campaign had dragged on without decision, and the emperor wished to withdraw. The prince sent Feng Lun west to tell him, "The rebels hold much land, but their ties are loose and they cannot truly command one another; only Luoyang takes orders. Their schemes are spent and their strength broken—they are living from hour to hour.
value.literal: At the time the army had long been unable to achieve victory, and the Emperor wished to withdraw. The Prince sent Lun west to see the Emperor and say, "Though the rebels' territory is vast, they are loosely bound and cannot command one another; the one who receives their orders is Luoyang alone. Their plans are exhausted and their strength spent—death is imminent.

value.zh: 今解而西，則賊勢磐結，後難以圖。」
value.en: If we pull back now, the enemy will knit their power together, and we shall never overcome them later."
value.literal: If we disengage now and march west, the rebels' strength will become firmly knit, and later it will be hard to overcome them."

value.zh: 帝納之。
value.en: The emperor accepted his counsel.
value.literal: The Emperor accepted this.

value.zh: 賊平，帝謂侍臣曰：「始議東討，時多沮解者，唯秦王謂必克，倫贊其行，雖張華葉策晉武，亦何以加於是！」
value.en: After the rebels were crushed, the emperor told his ministers, "When we first debated the eastern campaign, most men tried to dissuade me; only the Prince of Qin insisted we would prevail, and Feng Lun backed him. Not even Zhang Hua's counsel to Emperor Wu of Jin could outshine that!"
value.literal: When the rebels were pacified, the Emperor said to his attending ministers, "When we first debated the eastern campaign, many discouraged it, but only Prince Qin said victory was certain, and Lun endorsed his plan—even Zhang Hua's counsel to Emperor Wu of Jin could not surpass this!"

value.zh: 封平原縣公，判天策府司馬。
value.en: Feng Lun was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan County and appointed acting chief administrator of the Heavenly Stratagem Office.
value.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan County and made Acting Chief Administrator of the Heavenly Stratagem Office.

value.zh: 初，竇建德援洛，王將趣虎牢，倫與蕭瑀諫不可，至是入賀。
value.en: Earlier, when Dou Jiande marched to relieve Luoyang, the prince had meant to rush to Hulao; Feng Lun and Xiao Yu had urged against it. Now they came to offer their congratulations.
value.literal: Earlier, when Dou Jiande came to aid Luoyang, the Prince was about to hurry to Hulao; Feng Lun and Xiao Yu remonstrated that it should not be done. At this point they came in to offer congratulations.

value.zh: 王笑曰：「不用公言，今日幸而捷，豈智者千慮或有失乎？」
value.en: The prince smiled and said, "Had I listened to you, I might never have won today. Even the wisest man, planning a thousand times, can still miss once, can he not?"
value.literal: The Prince smiled and said, "Had I not taken your advice, today I would fortunately have won—can even the wise, in a thousand considerations, sometimes err?"

value.zh: 倫謝素不及。
value.en: Feng Lun apologized that he could not measure up to Yang Su.
value.literal: Lun apologized that he was not the equal of Su.

value.zh: 頃之，突厥寇太原，且遣使和親。
value.en: Soon afterward the Turks raided Taiyuan and at the same time sent envoys to propose a marriage alliance.
value.literal: Before long, the Turks raided Taiyuan and also sent envoys proposing a marriage alliance.

value.zh: 帝問計，群臣咸請許之可紓戰。
value.en: The emperor asked his ministers for counsel, and all urged him to accept the offer and ease the fighting.
value.literal: The Emperor asked for counsel; the ministers all urged accepting it to relieve the war pressure.

value.zh: 倫曰：「不然。
value.en: Feng Lun said, "That would be a mistake.
value.literal: Lun said, "Not so.

value.zh: 彼有輕中國心，謂我不能戰，若乘其怠擊之，勢必勝，勝而後和，威德兩全。
value.en: They look down on the Middle Kingdom and think we dare not fight. Strike while they are careless and we are sure to win; make peace only after victory, and both authority and virtue will be intact.
value.literal: They harbor contempt for China, thinking we cannot fight. If we strike while they are slack, we are sure to win. After victory, then make peace—prestige and virtue both complete.

value.zh: 今雖不戰，後必復來。
value.en: Even if we do not fight now, they will come again.
value.literal: Even if we do not fight now, they will surely come again later.

value.zh: 臣以為擊之便。」
value.en: Your servant believes it is better to attack them."
value.literal: Your subject holds that striking them is advantageous."

value.zh: 詔可。
value.en: An edict approved his proposal.
value.literal: An edict approved this.

value.zh: 尋檢校吏部尚書，進封趙國公，徙密國。
value.en: Before long he was made acting Minister of Personnel, raised to Duke of Zhao, and his fief was moved to the state of Mi.
value.literal: Soon he was made Acting Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, advanced to Duke of Zhao, and transferred to the state of Mi.

value.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷
value.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83

value.zh: 賈后淫虐日甚，私於太醫令程據等；
value.en: Empress Jia's debauchery and cruelty grew worse by the day. She took Cheng Ju, Director of the Imperial Physicians, and others as private lovers;
value.literal: Empress Jia's debauchery and cruelty grew daily worse; she took private relations with the Director of the Imperial Physicians, Cheng Ju, and others;

value.zh: 又以簏箱載道上年少入宮，復恐其漏洩，往往殺之。
value.en: and she had young men smuggled into the palace in bamboo crates. Fearing exposure, she often had them killed afterward.
value.literal: she also used bamboo cases to bring in young men from the roads to the palace, and fearing leaks often killed them.

value.zh: 賈模恐禍及己，甚憂之。
value.en: Jia Mo feared the scandal would engulf him and was deeply alarmed.
value.literal: Jia Mo feared disaster would reach him and was deeply troubled.

value.zh: 裴頠與模及張華議廢后，更立謝淑妃。
value.en: Pei Wei discussed with Mo and Zhang Hua deposing the empress and elevating Lady Xie, the Pure Consort, in her stead.
value.literal: Pei Wei discussed with Mo and Zhang Hua deposing the empress and installing Lady Xie, the Pure Consort, in her place.

value.zh: 模、華皆曰：「主上自無廢黜之意，而吾等專行之，倘上心不以為然，將若之何！
value.en: Mo and Hua both objected: "The emperor himself has no wish to depose her. If we act on our own and he disapproves, what then?
value.literal: Mo and Hua both said: "Our lord himself has no intent to depose her; if we act on our own authority and his heart does not approve, what then shall we do!

value.zh: 且諸王方強，朋黨各異，恐一旦禍起，身死國危，無益社稷。」
value.en: Besides, the princes are strong and their factions divided. If trouble erupts, we may die and the realm fall into peril, with no gain for the state."
value.literal: Moreover the princes are now strong and their factions differ; we fear that if disaster should suddenly arise, we would die and the state be endangered, with no benefit to the altars of soil and grain."

value.zh: 頠曰：「誠如公言。
value.en: Pei replied: "You are right.
value.literal: Pei said: "It is indeed as you say.

value.zh: 然中宮逞其昏虐，亂可立待也。」
value.en: Yet the empress indulges her cruelty and folly. Chaos may come at any moment."
value.literal: Yet the central palace indulges its benighted cruelty; disorder may be awaited at once."

value.zh: 華曰：「卿二人於中宮皆親戚，言或見信，宜數為陳禍福之戒，庶無大悖，則天下尚未至於亂，吾曹得以估游卒歲而已。」
value.en: Zhang Hua said: "You are both related to the empress and may be heard. Warn her often of the consequences. If she avoids the worst excesses, the realm may yet hold together and we can live out our days in peace."
value.literal: Hua said: "You two are both kin to the central palace; your words may win belief. You ought often to set forth warnings of fortune and calamity, so that with luck there will be no great outrage; then the realm may not yet come to disorder, and we may idle through the year as merchants do."

value.zh: 頠旦夕說其從母廣城君，令戒諭賈后以親厚太子，賈模亦數為后言禍福；
value.en: Pei pressed his aunt, the Lady of Guangcheng, day and night to warn Empress Jia to treat the heir apparent kindly. Jia Mo likewise urged the empress repeatedly about the risks she was courting;
value.literal: Pei day and night urged his mother's younger sister, the Lady of Guangcheng, to admonish Empress Jia to treat the Heir Apparent with affection; Jia Mo also repeatedly spoke to the empress of fortune and calamity;

value.zh: 后不能用，反以模為毀己而疏之；
value.en: but she would not listen. She took Mo for a slanderer and estranged herself from him;
value.literal: the empress would not heed them and instead, taking Mo for one who slandered her, kept him at a distance;

value.zh: 模不得志，憂憤而卒。
value.en: and Mo, frustrated and despairing, died of grief.
value.literal: Mo, unable to achieve his aim, died of grief and anger.

value.zh: 裴頠薦平陽韋忠於張華，華辟之，忠辭疾不起。
value.en: Pei Wei recommended Wei Zhong of Pingyang to Zhang Hua. Hua summoned him, but Zhong pleaded illness and refused to serve.
value.literal: Pei Wei recommended Wei Zhong of Pingyang to Zhang Hua; Hua summoned him, but Zhong declined on grounds of illness and did not take office.

value.zh: 人問其故，忠曰：「張茂先華而不實，裴逸民欲而無厭，棄典禮而附賊後，此豈大丈夫之所為哉！
value.en: Asked why, Zhong said: "Zhang Hua is showy but hollow; Pei Wei is grasping and never satisfied. They abandon ritual and cling to the empress's faction. Is that the conduct of a true gentleman?
value.literal: When people asked his reason, Zhong said: "Zhang Maoxian is flowery but not solid; Pei Yimin is covetous and never satisfied. They abandon canonical rites and attach themselves to the empress's faction—is this what a great man should do!

value.zh: 逸民每有心托我，我常恐其溺於深淵而餘波及我，況可褰裳而就之哉！」
value.en: Wei keeps trying to draw me in. I always fear that if he falls into the abyss the splash will reach me. How could I wade in after him!"
value.literal: Yimin often wishes to entrust affairs to me; I constantly fear that if he falls into the deep abyss the dregs will splash upon me—how much less could I lift my robe and go to him!"

value.zh: 於時朝野咸知賈后有害太子之意，中護軍趙俊請太子廢后，太子不聽。
value.en: By then everyone knew Empress Jia meant to destroy the heir apparent. Zhao Jun, Central Protector of the Army, urged him to depose her, but he refused.
value.literal: At that time court and commonalty alike knew Empress Jia meant harm to the Heir Apparent; the Central Protector of the Army Zhao Jun asked the Heir Apparent to depose the empress, but the Heir Apparent would not listen.

value.zh: 左衛率東平劉卞，以賈后之謀問張華，華曰：「不聞。」
value.en: Liu Bian of Dongping, Colonel of the Left Guards, asked Zhang Hua about the empress's plot. Hua said, "I have heard nothing."
value.literal: Liu Bian of Dongping, Colonel of the Left Guards, asked Zhang Hua about Empress Jia's plot; Hua said: "I have not heard of it."

value.zh: 卞曰：「卞自須昌小吏，受公成拔以至今日。
value.en: Bian said, "I was only a petty clerk in Xuchang until you raised me to what I am today.
value.literal: Bian said: "Bian rose from a petty clerk in Xuchang through your grace's full promotion to reach today.

value.zh: 士感知己，是以盡言，而公更有疑於卞邪！」
value.en: A gentleman repays his patron with full candor. Do you still doubt me?"
value.literal: A gentleman who knows gratitude to his patron therefore speaks fully—yet does Your Excellency still doubt Bian!"

value.zh: 華曰：「假令有此，君欲如何？」
value.en: Hua asked, "Suppose it were true. What would you do?"
value.literal: Hua said: "Suppose there were such a thing—what would you intend?"

value.zh: 卞曰：「東宮俊乂如林，四率精兵萬人；
value.en: Bian said, "The Eastern Palace has talent in abundance, and the four colonels command ten thousand elite troops.
value.literal: Bian said: "The Eastern Palace has talented men like a forest; the four colonels command elite troops of ten thousand;

value.zh: 公居阿衡之任，若得公命，皇太子因朝入錄尚書事，廢賈后於金墉城，兩黃門力耳。」
value.en: You hold the chief minister's power. With your order the heir apparent could enter court, take charge of the Masters of Writing, and depose Empress Jia at Jinyong. It would take only two Yellow Gate attendants."
value.literal: Your Excellency holds the office of chief minister; if we obtain your command, the Heir Apparent can enter at court to record the Masters of Writing affairs and depose Empress Jia at Jinyong—it is only the strength of two Yellow Gate attendants."

value.zh: 華曰：「今天子當陽，太子，人子也，吾又不受阿衡之命，忽相與行此，是無君父而以不孝示天下也。
value.en: Hua said, "The emperor reigns in his own right. The heir apparent is his son, and I have received no commission as chief minister. To act suddenly in this way would be to cast aside ruler and father and show the world an act of filial impiety.
value.literal: Hua said: "Today the Son of Heaven faces the sun; the Heir Apparent is a human son, and I have not received the chief minister's commission—suddenly to act together in this would be to have no ruler or father and display filial impiety to the realm.

value.zh: 雖能有成，猶不免罪。
value.en: Even if we succeeded, we would still be guilty.
value.literal: Even if we could succeed, we would still not escape guilt.

value.zh: 況權戚滿朝，威柄不一，成可必乎？」
value.en: Besides, powerful kin fill the court and power is divided. Can success be certain?"
value.literal: Moreover the powerful kin fill the court and authority is not unified—can success be certain?"

value.zh: 賈后常使親黨微服聽察於外，頗聞卞言，乃遷卞為雍州刺史；
value.en: Empress Jia often had her kin spy in disguise and learned of Bian's words. She transferred him to Inspector of Yongzhou;
value.literal: Empress Jia often had her kin in plain dress listen and observe outside and heard much of Bian's words; she thereupon transferred Bian to be Inspector of Yongzhou;

value.zh: 卞知言洩，飲藥而死。
value.en: and Bian, knowing his plot had leaked, took poison and died.
value.literal: Bian, knowing his words had leaked, took poison and died.

value.zh: 壬戌，帝幸式乾殿，召公卿入，使黃門令董猛以太子書及青紙詔示之曰：「遹書如此，今賜死。」
value.en: On the day renxu the emperor went to the Shiqian Hall and summoned the ministers. Yellow Gate Commandant Dong Meng showed them the heir apparent's letter and a blue-paper edict, saying: "Yu wrote this. He is to die."
value.literal: On the day renxu the emperor visited the Shiqian Hall, summoned the excellencies and ministers in, and had the Yellow Gate Commandant Dong Meng show them the Heir Apparent's letter and the blue-paper edict, saying: "Yu's letter is thus—now grant death."

value.zh: 遍示諸公王，莫有言者。
value.en: He showed it to all the princes and nobles. No one spoke.
value.literal: He showed it to all the princes and lords; none spoke.

value.zh: 張華曰：「此國之大禍，自古以來，常因廢黜正嫡以致喪亂。
value.en: Zhang Hua said, "This is a great calamity for the state. Since antiquity disorder has often followed the deposition of the legitimate heir.
value.literal: Zhang Hua said: "This is a great calamity for the state. Since antiquity disorder has often come from deposing the legitimate heir.

value.zh: 且國家有天下日淺，願陛下詳之！」
value.en: Moreover the dynasty has held the realm only a short time. I beg Your Majesty to consider carefully!"
value.literal: Moreover the state has held the realm but a short time—I beg Your Majesty to consider carefully!"

value.zh: 裴頠以為宜先檢校傳書者，又請比較太子手書，不然，恐有詐妄。
value.en: Pei Wei urged that the messenger be examined first and the handwriting compared with the heir apparent's own script, lest the letter be a forgery.
value.literal: Pei Wei held that one ought first to examine and verify the person who transmitted the letter, and also requested comparison with the Heir Apparent's own handwriting; otherwise he feared there might be fraud.

value.zh: 賈后乃出太子啟事十餘紙，眾人比視，亦無敢言非者。
value.en: Empress Jia then produced more than ten sheets of the heir apparent's memorials. When the assembly compared them, no one dared say they did not match.
value.literal: Empress Jia then produced more than ten sheets of the Heir Apparent's memorials; when the assembly compared them, none dared say they did not match.

value.zh: 賈后使董猛矯以長廣公主辭白帝曰：「事宜速決，而群臣各不同，其不從詔者，宜以軍法從事。」
value.en: Empress Jia had Dong Meng report to the emperor in the name of the Princess of Changguang: "This must be decided at once. The ministers are divided. Those who disobey the edict should be dealt with by military law."
value.literal: Empress Jia had Dong Meng, falsely in the name of the Princess of Changguang, report to the emperor: "The affair ought to be decided quickly, yet the ministers all differ; those who do not follow the edict ought to be handled by military law."

value.zh: 議至日西，不決。
value.en: Debate continued until sunset without resolution.
value.literal: Deliberation continued until the sun was in the west, without decision.

value.zh: 后見華等意堅，懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。
value.en: Seeing Zhang Hua and the others hold firm and fearing the plot might fail, the empress memorialized to depose the heir apparent as a commoner. The edict was approved.
value.literal: The empress, seeing that Hua and the others were firm in intent and fearing the affair might change, submitted a memorial to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner; an edict approved it.

value.zh: 於是使尚書和郁等持節詣東宮，廢太子為庶人，太子改服出，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車，車武公澹以兵仗送太子及妃王氏、三子虨、臧、尚同幽於金墉城。
value.en: He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace. The heir apparent changed his garments, bowed twice, received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart. Sima Dan, Marquis of Chewu, escorted him with armed guards, together with his consort Lady Wang and his three sons Xian, Zang, and Shang, to confinement at Jinyong.
value.literal: Thereupon He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner. The Heir Apparent changed his garments and came out, bowed twice and received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, rode a rough ox-cart, and the Marquis of Chewu, Sima Dan, with arms escorted the Heir Apparent, his consort Lady Wang, and his three sons Xian, Zang, and Shang together to be confined at Jinyong.

value.zh: 王衍自表離婚，許之，妃慟哭而歸。
value.en: Wang Yan memorialized to divorce her, and permission was granted. The consort returned home in bitter tears.
value.literal: Wang Yan himself submitted a memorial requesting divorce; it was granted, and the consort returned home weeping bitterly.

value.zh: 殺太子母謝淑媛及虨母保林蔣俊。
value.en: The heir apparent's mother, Lady Xie the Gracious Lady, and Xian's mother, Forest Keeper Jiang Jun, were executed.
value.literal: The Heir Apparent's mother, the Gracious Lady Xie, and Xian's mother, the Forest Keeper Jiang Jun, were killed.

value.zh: 三月，尉氏雨血，妖星見南方，太白晝見，中台星拆。
value.en: In the third month blood rained at Weishi, an ominous star appeared in the south, Venus was seen by day, and the Central Terrace star split.
value.literal: In the third month blood rained at Weishi, an ominous star appeared in the south, the Great White was seen by day, and the Central Terrace star split.

value.zh: 張華少子韙勸華遜位，華不從，曰：「天道幽遠，不如靜以待之。」
value.en: Hua's younger son Wei urged him to resign; Hua refused, saying: "Heaven's way is obscure. Better to wait quietly."
value.literal: Zhang Hua's younger son Wei urged Hua to yield his post; Hua would not, saying: "The Way of Heaven is remote and obscure—better to wait quietly."

value.zh: 太子既廢，眾情憤怒。
value.en: Once the heir apparent was deposed, public anger boiled over.
value.literal: Once the Heir Apparent was deposed, public sentiment was furious.

value.zh: 有衛督司馬雅、常從督許超，皆嘗給事東宮，與殿中郎士猗等謀廢賈后，復太子。
value.en: Sima Ya, Colonel of the Guards, and Xu Chao, Regular Colonel of the Followers, both former Eastern Palace attendants, joined Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others to plot deposing Empress Jia and restoring the heir apparent.
value.literal: The Colonel of the Guards Sima Ya and the Regular Colonel of the Followers Xu Chao, who had both once served the Eastern Palace, joined the Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others in plotting to depose Empress Jia and restore the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 以張華、裴頠安常保位，難與行權，右軍將軍趙王倫執兵柄，性貪冒，可假以濟事。
value.en: They judged Zhang Hua and Pei Wei too cautious to act, while Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, held the armies and was greedy—he could be used.
value.literal: They judged Zhang Hua and Pei Wei content to preserve their posts and hard to move to action, while the General of the Right Army the Prince of Zhao Sima Lun held military power and was greedy—he could be borrowed to accomplish the affair.

value.zh: 乃說孫秀曰：「中宮凶妒無道，與賈謐等共誣廢太子。
value.en: They told Sun Xiu: "The empress is vicious and lawless. With Jia Mi she framed and deposed the heir apparent.
value.literal: They thereupon said to Sun Xiu: "The central palace is fierce, jealous, and without the Way, and together with Jia Mi and others falsely deposed the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 今國無嫡嗣，社稷將危，大臣將起大事，而公名奉事中宮，與賈、郭親善，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一朝事起，禍必相及，何不先謀之乎！」
value.en: The realm lacks a legitimate heir and the altars are endangered. Great ministers will act, yet you serve the empress and are close to the Jia and Guo clans. When the heir apparent fell, men said you knew beforehand. When trouble erupts you will not escape—why not strike first?"
value.literal: Now the state has no legitimate heir and the altars are in peril; the great ministers will raise a great affair, yet you by name attend the central palace and are intimate with the Jia and Guo—when the Heir Apparent was deposed all said you foreknew it. Once trouble rises disaster must reach you—why not plot first!"

value.zh: 秀許諾，言於倫，倫納焉，遂告通事令史張林及省事張衡等，使為內應。
value.en: Xiu agreed and told Lun, who accepted and enlisted Zhang Lin and Zhang Heng as inside agents.
value.literal: Xiu promised and spoke to Lun; Lun accepted, and reported to the clerks Zhang Lin and Zhang Heng among the communications staff to serve as inside agents.

value.zh: 趙王倫、孫秀將討賈后，告右衛佽飛督閭和，和從之，期以癸巳丙夜一籌，以鼓聲為應。
value.en: Lun and Xiu prepared to move against the empress, won over Lü He, Colonel of the Right Guards Attendants, and set guisi night, second watch of the bing hour, drums as signal.
value.literal: The Prince of Zhao Lun and Sun Xiu were about to attack Empress Jia; they told the Colonel of the Right Guards Attendants Lü He, who joined them, fixing the night of guisi on the second watch of the bing hour, with drumbeats as signal.

value.zh: 癸巳，秀使司馬雅告張華曰：「趙王欲與公共匡社稷，為天下除害，使雅以告。」
value.en: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join you to save the realm and remove this evil."
value.literal: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join with you to steady the altars, remove harm for the realm—Ya reports this."

value.zh: 華拒之。
value.en: Hua refused.
value.literal: Hua refused.

value.zh: 雅怒曰：「刃將加頸，猶為是言邪！」
value.en: Ya snapped: "The blade is at your neck and you still talk like that!"
value.literal: Ya angrily said: "The blade is at the neck—yet you speak thus!"

value.zh: 不顧而出。
value.en: He strode out without a backward glance.
value.literal: He left without looking back.

value.zh: 及期，倫矯詔敕三部司馬曰：「中宮與賈謐等殺吾太子，今使車騎入廢中宮，汝等皆當從命，事畢，賜爵關中侯，不從者誅三族。」
value.en: At the hour Lun forged an edict to the three departments: "The empress and Jia Mi killed the heir apparent. The Cavalry General enters to depose her. Obey and receive marquisates; disobey and face extermination."
value.literal: When the hour came Lun forged an edict instructing the three departments' majors: "The central palace and Jia Mi and others killed our Heir Apparent; the Cavalry General will enter and depose the central palace—you must all obey. When done, enfeoffment as marquis within the passes; disobedience exterminates three clans."

value.zh: 眾皆從之。
value.en: All obeyed.
value.literal: All obeyed.

value.zh: 又矯詔開門，夜入，陳兵道南，遣翊軍校尉齊王冏將百人排冏而入，華林令駱休為內應，迎帝幸東堂，以詔召賈謐於殿前，將誅之。
value.en: He forged orders to open the gates, entered at night, lined troops along the southern route, sent Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, with a hundred men to force entry, Luo Xiu of Hualin as inside agent, escorted the emperor to the Eastern Hall, and summoned Jia Mi to execution.
value.literal: He also forged an edict to open the gates, entered by night, arrayed troops along the southern way, sent the Colonel of the Supports the Prince of Qi Sima Jiong with a hundred men to force the gates and enter, the Commandant of the Hualin Park Luo Xiu as inside agent, brought the emperor to the Eastern Hall, and by edict summoned Jia Mi before the hall to be executed.

value.zh: 謐走入西鐘下，呼曰：「阿后救我！」
value.en: Mi fled to the western bell-frame crying: "Mother, save me!"
value.literal: Mi ran beneath the western bell-frame crying: "Mother, save me!"

value.zh: 就斬之。
value.en: He was beheaded at once.
value.literal: He was beheaded on the spot.

value.zh: 賈后見齊王冏，驚曰：「卿何為來？」
value.en: Seeing Sima Jiong the empress cried: "Why are you here?"
value.literal: When Empress Jia saw Sima Jiong she exclaimed: "Why have you come?"

value.zh: 冏曰：「有詔收后。」
value.en: Jiong said: "An edict commands your arrest."
value.literal: Jiong said: "There is an edict to take the empress."

value.zh: 后曰：「詔當從我出，何詔也！」
value.en: She said: "Edicts should come from me—what edict is this!"
value.literal: The empress said: "Edicts should come from me—what edict is this!"

value.zh: 后至上閤，遙呼帝曰：「陛下有婦，使人廢之，亦行自廢矣。」
value.en: She climbed to the upper pavilion and called to the emperor: "You have a wife; when others depose her, you will be deposed yourself."
value.literal: She went up to the upper pavilion and called to the emperor from afar: "Your Majesty has a consort; when others deposed her, you too will be deposed."

value.zh: 是時，梁王肜亦預其謀，后問冏曰：「起事者誰？」
value.en: The Prince of Liang Sima Rong was also in the plot; she asked Jiong: "Who raised this?"
value.literal: At that time the Prince of Liang Sima Rong also took part in the plot; the empress asked Jiong: "Who raised the affair?"

value.zh: 冏曰：「梁、趙。」
value.en: Jiong said: "Liang and Zhao."
value.literal: Jiong said: "Liang and Zhao."

value.zh: 后曰：「系狗當繫頸，反系其尾，何得不然！」
value.en: She said: "Tie a dog by the neck, not the tail—was this not inevitable!"
value.literal: The empress said: "When tying a dog one should tie the neck—instead they tied the tail; how could it not turn out thus!"

value.zh: 遂廢后為庶人，幽之於建始殿，收趙粲、賈午等付暴室考竟。
value.en: She was deposed as a commoner and confined in the Jianshi Hall; Zhao Can, Jia Wu, and others were sent to the Severe Chamber for interrogation unto death.
value.literal: She was thereupon deposed as commoner and confined in the Jianshi Hall; Zhao Can, Jia Wu, and others were taken to the Severe Chamber for interrogation to the death.

value.zh: 詔尚書收捕賈氏親黨，召中書監、侍中、黃門侍郎、八座皆夜入殿。
value.en: An edict ordered arrest of the Jia clan; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and Eight Seats were summoned at night.
value.literal: An edict ordered the Masters of Writing to arrest the Jia kin; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and the Eight Seats were all summoned into the hall at night.

value.zh: 尚書始疑詔有詐，郎師景露版奏請手詔，倫等斬之以徇。
value.en: The Masters of Writing doubted the edict; Gentleman Shi Jing asked for the emperor's own hand; Lun beheaded him as warning.
value.literal: The Masters of Writing at first doubted the edict was false; Gentleman Shi Jing displayed the tablet and asked for a handwritten edict; Lun and the rest beheaded him as a warning.

value.zh: 倫陰與秀謀篡位，欲先除朝望，且報宿怨，乃執張華、裴頠、解系、解結等於殿前。
value.en: Lun secretly plotted usurpation with Xiu, first removing leading ministers and settling old scores; he seized Zhang Hua, Pei Wei, Xie Ji, Xie Jie, and others in the hall.
value.literal: Lun secretly plotted with Xiu to usurp the throne, wishing first to remove men of court esteem and also settle old scores; he seized Zhang Hua, Pei Wei, Xie Ji, Xie Jie, and others before the hall.

value.zh: 華謂張林曰：「卿欲害忠臣邪？」
value.en: Hua said to Zhang Lin: "Do you mean to kill loyal ministers?"
value.literal: Hua said to Zhang Lin: "Do you wish to harm loyal ministers?"

value.zh: 林稱詔詰之曰：「卿為宰相，太子之廢，不能死節，何也？」
value.en: Lin, citing the edict, demanded: "As chief minister, when the heir apparent was deposed why did you not die for principle?"
value.literal: Lin, claiming the edict, interrogated him: "You were chief minister; when the Heir Apparent was deposed you could not die for principle—why?"

value.zh: 華曰：「式乾之議，臣諫事具存，可覆按也。」
value.en: Hua said: "My remonstrance at the Shiqian deliberation is on record and may be reviewed."
value.literal: Hua said: "On the deliberation at Shiqian my remonstrance is fully recorded and may be reviewed."

value.zh: 林曰：「諫而不從，何不去位？」
value.en: Lin said: "If remonstrance failed, why not resign?"
value.literal: Lin said: "If you remonstrated and were not obeyed, why not leave office?"

value.zh: 華無以對。
value.en: Hua had no answer.
value.literal: Hua had no reply.

value.zh: 遂皆斬之，仍夷三族。
value.en: All were beheaded and their clans exterminated to the third degree.
value.literal: They were all beheaded and their clans exterminated to the third degree.

value.zh: 解結女適裴氏，明日當嫁而禍起，裴氏欲認活之，女曰：「家既若此，我何以活為！」
value.en: Xie Jie's daughter was to marry into the Pei clan next day when disaster struck; the Peis wished to save her; she said: "With my house destroyed, how can I live!"
value.literal: Xie Jie's daughter was betrothed to the Pei clan; the wedding was due the next day when disaster struck; the Pei wished to claim her alive; the girl said: "With my house thus, how can I live!"

value.zh: 亦坐死。
value.en: She died as well.
value.literal: She too died for it.

value.zh: 朝廷由是議革舊制，女不從死。
value.en: The court then debated abolishing the old rule that wives and daughters die with the clan.
value.literal: The court thereupon debated abolishing the old rule that daughters follow their kin to death.

value.zh: 甲午，倫坐端門，遣尚書和郁持節送賈庶人於金墉；
value.en: On jiawu Lun sat at the Duan Gate and sent He Yu with credentials to convey the deposed empress to Jinyong;
value.literal: On the day jiawu Lun sat at the Duan Gate and sent the Masters of Writing He Yu with credentials to convey the deposed Jia commoner to Jinyong;

value.zh: 誅劉振、董猛、孫慮、程據等；
value.en: Liu Zhen, Dong Meng, Sun Lv, Cheng Ju, and others were executed;
value.literal: Liu Zhen, Dong Meng, Sun Lv, Cheng Ju, and others were executed;

value.zh: 司徒王戎及內外官坐張、裴親黨黜免者甚眾。
value.en: Minister over the Masses Wang Rong and many inner and outer officials were dismissed as kin to Zhang and Pei.
value.literal: the Minister over the Masses Wang Rong and inner and outer officials dismissed as kin to Zhang and Pei were very numerous.

value.zh: 閻纘撫張華屍慟哭曰：「早語君遜位而不肯，今果不免，命也！」
value.en: Yan Xun stroked Zhang Hua's corpse and wailed: "I urged you to resign and you would not; now you could not escape—fate!"
value.literal: Yan Xun stroked Zhang Hua's corpse and wailed: "I told you early to yield your post and you would not; now you could not escape—fate!"

value.zh: 孫秀議加相國倫九錫，百官莫敢異議。
value.en: Xiu proposed granting Lun the Nine Bestowals; no official dared object.
value.literal: Sun Xiu proposed granting Chancellor Lun the Nine Bestowals; the hundred officials dared not dissent.

value.zh: 吏部尚書劉頌曰：「昔漢之錫魏，魏之錫晉，皆一時之用，非可通行。
value.en: Liu Song, Director of Personnel, said: "When Han bestowed them on Wei and Wei on Jin, those were expedients of the moment, not universal precedent.
value.literal: Liu Song, Director of Personnel, said: "In the past Han bestowed them on Wei and Wei on Jin—all were expedients of the moment and cannot be made universal practice.

value.zh: 周勃、霍光，其功至大，皆不聞有九錫之命也。」
value.en: Zhou Bo and Huo Guang achieved the greatest merit, yet never received the Nine Bestowals."
value.literal: Zhou Bo and Huo Guang achieved the greatest merit, yet one never hears of commands granting the Nine Bestowals."

value.zh: 張林積忿不已，以頌為張華之黨，將殺之。
value.en: Zhang Lin, still furious, treated Song as Zhang Hua's partisan and meant to kill him.
value.literal: Zhang Lin, nursing his wrath, took Song for a partisan of Zhang Hua and was about to kill him.

value.zh: 孫秀曰：「殺張、裴已傷時望，不可復殺頌。」
value.en: Xiu said: "Killing Zhang and Pei has already harmed public esteem. We cannot kill Song too."
value.literal: Sun Xiu said: "Killing Zhang and Pei has already harmed the age's esteem—we cannot kill Song again."

value.zh: 林乃止。
value.en: Lin desisted.
value.literal: Lin thereupon stopped.

value.zh: 以頌為光祿大夫。
value.en: Song was made Household Grandee.
value.literal: Song was made Household Grandee.

value.zh: 遂下詔加倫九錫，復加其子荂撫軍將軍，虔中軍將軍，詡為侍中。
value.en: An edict granted Lun the Nine Bestowals and further made Fu General of the Guards, Qian Central Commander, and Xu Attendant.
value.literal: An edict was then issued granting Lun the Nine Bestowals; his son Fu was further made General of the Guards, Qian Central Commander of the Army, and Xu Attendant.

value.zh: 又加孫秀侍中、輔國將軍，相國司馬、右率如故。
value.en: Xiu was made Attendant and General Who Assists the State, retaining his posts as Chancellor's Major and Colonel of the Right.
value.literal: Sun Xiu was further made Attendant and General Who Assists the State, retaining his posts as Chancellor's Major and Colonel of the Right.

value.zh: 張林等並居顯要。
value.en: Zhang Lin and others all held prominent posts.
value.literal: Zhang Lin and the rest all held prominent posts.

value.zh: 增相府兵為二萬人，與宿衛同，並所隱匿之兵，數逾三萬。
value.en: Chancellor household troops were raised to twenty thousand, equal to the palace guard; with hidden forces the total exceeded thirty thousand.
value.literal: The chancellor's household troops were increased to twenty thousand, equal to the palace guard, and with hidden troops as well the number exceeded thirty thousand.
